Cologne / Köln 98

Dom · Altstadt · Ehrenfeld · Südstadt

  1. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Kölner Dom

    Cologne's Gothic cathedral of St Peter, begun 1248 and completed 1880, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Germany's most-visited landmark. Climb the 533 steps of the south tower for the city view; inside are the Shrine of the Three Kings and the Gerhard Richter window.

    Look for Gothic cathedral, UNESCO

    Domkloster 4, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Deutsche UNESCO-Kommission, KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com

  2. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Groß St. Martin

    The tall crossing tower of this Romanesque basilica dominates the Rhine-side Altstadt skyline beside the Fischmarkt. One of Cologne's twelve great Romanesque churches, rebuilt after WWII.

    Look for Romanesque basilica

    An Groß St. Martin 9, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Förderverein Romanische Kirchen Köln, KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com

  3. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    St. Gereon

    A former collegiate church whose extraordinary ten-sided ribbed decagon (c. 1220) is one of the largest domed spaces built between antiquity and the Renaissance. Among the twelve Romanesque churches.

    Look for Romanesque decagon

    Gereonsdriesch 2-4, 50670 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Förderverein Romanische Kirchen Köln, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    St. Maria im Kapitol

    Built on the Roman capitol, this 11th-century church has a rare trefoil east end and famous carved wooden doors of c. 1065. One of the twelve Romanesque churches and among the finest.

    Look for Romanesque, carved doors

    Kasinostraße 6, 50676 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Förderverein Romanische Kirchen Köln, KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com

  5. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Museum Ludwig

    One of Europe's great collections of 20th- and 21st-century art beside the Dom: the largest Pop Art holdings outside the US, a major Picasso collection and Russian avant-garde.

    Look for Modern & Pop Art

    Heinrich-Böll-Platz, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Museen der Stadt Köln, KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com

  6. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Wallraf-Richartz-Museum & Fondation Corboud

    Cologne's oldest museum, spanning medieval Cologne panel painting through Rubens, Rembrandt and a superb Impressionist and Post-Impressionist gallery (Fondation Corboud).

    Look for Old Masters to Impressionism

    Obenmarspforten 40, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Wallraf-Richartz-Museum & Fondation Corboud, KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com

  7. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Römisch-Germanisches Museum

    Cologne's Roman archaeology museum (temporarily in the Belgisches Haus during renovation), showing the Dionysus mosaic, the Poblicius tomb and everyday finds from Roman Colonia.

    Look for Roman archaeology

    Cäcilienstraße 46, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Museen der Stadt Köln, KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com

  8. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Schokoladenmuseum

    A glass ship-shaped museum at the tip of the Rheinauhafen tracing 4,000 years of chocolate, with a working production line and a chocolate fountain. One of Cologne's most popular attractions.

    Look for Chocolate museum

    Am Schokoladenmuseum 1a, 50678 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com, koeln.de (Stadtportal)

  9. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Kolumba

    The Archdiocese's art museum, Peter Zumthor's celebrated building rising over the ruins of the Gothic St Kolumba church and its 1950 'Madonna of the Ruins' chapel; sacred and contemporary art shown together.

    Look for Zumthor architecture, art

    Kolumbastraße 4, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Kolumba – Kunstmuseum des Erzbistums Köln, KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com

  10. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    NS-Dokumentationszentrum (EL-DE-Haus)

    The former Cologne Gestapo headquarters, now a memorial and documentation centre; the preserved basement prison cells still carry hundreds of prisoners' wall inscriptions.

    Look for Nazi-era memorial

    Appellhofplatz 23-25, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by Museen der Stadt Köln, Stadt Köln (offiziell)

  11. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Historisches Rathaus

    Germany's oldest city hall, with a Gothic council tower carrying 124 sculptures and an elegant Renaissance loggia facing the Alter Markt; a carillon rings out daily.

    Look for Historic town hall

    Rathausplatz 2, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com, Stadt Köln (offiziell)

  12. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Hohenzollernbrücke

    The great rail-and-pedestrian arch bridge behind the Dom, whose fences carry hundreds of thousands of love locks; the classic vantage for the cathedral-and-Rhine skyline.

    Hohenzollernbrücke, 50667 Köln, Germany

  13. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Kranhäuser

  15. Must see · Cologne / Köln

    Ehrenfeld

  16. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Cologne / Köln

    Früh am Dom

    The definitive Dom-side Brauhaus, brewing since 1904, where Köbes in blue aprons serve Früh Kölsch by the stange and the Halve Hahn (rye roll with aged Gouda) is a rite of passage. Vast warren of vaulted rooms.

    Am Hof 12-18, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by KölnTourismus / cologne-tourism.com, koeln.de (Stadtportal)

  17. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Cologne / Köln

    Brauerei zur Malzmühle

    A family brewery on the Heumarkt since 1858 pouring the maltier Mühlen Kölsch, and one of the best places for Himmel un Ääd (black pudding with mashed potato and apple). Voted among Cologne's favourite Brauhäuser.

    Heumarkt 6, 50667 Köln, Germany

    Recommended by koeln.de (Stadtportal), t-online Köln

  18. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Cologne / Köln

    Brauhaus Päffgen

    A cult Brauhaus in the Friesenviertel brewing Päffgen Kölsch since 1883 and still tapping it from wooden barrels; topped a reader poll of Cologne's favourite Brauhaus. Leafy back courtyard.

    Friesenstraße 64-66, 50670 Köln, Germany

Bonn 44

Beethoven · Museumsmeile · Bad Godesberg

  1. Must see · Bonn

    Beethoven-Haus

    Ludwig van Beethoven's birthplace and one of the most-visited music museums in the world, holding the largest Beethoven collection anywhere. Founded 1889; the neighbouring houses hold the Beethoven archive, library and a chamber-music hall.

    Look for Beethoven's birthplace

    Bonngasse 20, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.)

  2. Must see · Bonn

    Bonner Münster

    Bonn's Romanesque landmark basilica (11th–13th c.), raised over the graves of the martyrs Cassius and Florentius and carried in the city seal since the 13th century. Given the title Basilica minor in 1956; reopened October 2021 after a full restoration.

    Look for 12th-c. Romanesque basilica

    Gerhard-von-Are-Straße 5, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Bonn

    Bundeskunsthalle

    The federal art and exhibitions hall, a Gustav Peichl building (1992) whose three blue cone-skylights and rooftop sculpture garden are a Museumsmeile signature. Big rotating shows spanning art, archaeology and culture.

    Look for Peichl building · major touring shows

    Friedrich-Ebert-Allee 4, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, baukunst-nrw, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Bonn

    Poppelsdorfer Schloss & Botanischer Garten

    The Rococo pleasure palace of the Cologne prince-electors (completed 1746), now a university building, wrapped by the Botanical Garden — one of the oldest and most traditional north of the Alps, with an Amorphophallus titanum among its stars. Garden admission free.

    Look for Rococo palace · botanical garden

    Meckenheimer Allee 171, 53115 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), Official site of the place, Wikipedia

  5. Must see · Bonn

    Haus der Geschichte

    The museum of postwar German history, the anchor of Bonn's Museumsmeile and one of the country's most-visited museums. Free admission; a vivid, hands-on walk through the Bundesrepublik from 1945 to today.

    Look for Postwar German history · free

    Willy-Brandt-Allee 14, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region

  6. Must see · Bonn

    Museum Koenig

    The Zoologisches Forschungsmuseum Alexander Koenig, a natural-history museum famous for its walk-through African savannah dioramas. In 1948 its festival hall hosted the Parlamentarischer Rat that drafted the Grundgesetz, giving the Federal Republic its birthplace here.

    Look for Natural history · birthplace of the Grundgesetz

    Adenauerallee 160, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Wikipedia

  7. Must see · Bonn

    Altes Rathaus & Markt

    Bonn's pink-and-gold Rococo town hall (1737–38, from a design by Michael Leveilly), its gilded perron a stage for de Gaulle, Kennedy and Gorbachev. It presides over the daily market square at the city's heart.

    Look for Rococo town hall · market square

    Markt 2, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital)

  8. Must see · Bonn

    Freizeitpark Rheinaue

    Bonn's 160-hectare riverside park, laid out for the 1979 Bundesgartenschau, with a lake, a Japanese garden, rose garden and 45 km of paths. A vast green lung for cycling, picnics and the big summer flea market.

    Look for Bundesgartenschau park · Japanese garden

    Ludwig-Erhard-Allee 20, 53175 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.)

  9. Must see · Bonn

    Alter Zoll

    A 17th-century bastion of the old city wall, below the university's Hofgarten, turned into Bonn's classic Rhine viewpoint. From its platform the river bends toward the peaks of the Siebengebirge — a favourite of Romantic painters.

    Look for Rhine-bastion viewpoint

    Brassertufer 1, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Wikipedia

  10. Must see · Bonn

    Kurfürstliches Schloss & Hofgarten

    The former electoral palace (1697–1705), a vast Baroque residence that has been the main building of the University of Bonn since 1818. Its sweeping Hofgarten lawn is the students' and city's great open-air meeting place.

    Look for Baroque palace · university · park

    Regina-Pacis-Weg 3, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital)

  11. Must see · Bonn

    Drachenfels & Drachenfelsbahn

    The most-climbed mountain in Europe, crowned by a ruined 12th-century castle with a sweeping Rhine panorama across the Siebengebirge. Ride Germany's oldest rack railway (1883) up from Königswinter — an easy edge day-trip from Bonn across the river.

    Look for Siebengebirge summit · rack railway

    Drachenfelsstraße 53, 53639 Königswinter, Germany

    Recommended by NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Official site of the place

  12. Must see · Bonn

    Schloss Drachenburg

    A fairy-tale Gründerzeit palace (1882–84) perched on the Drachenfels slope, all turrets, terraces and stained glass, with grand river views. Reached on foot or by an intermediate stop of the Drachenfels railway.

    Look for Gründerzeit fantasy castle

    Drachenfelsstraße 118, 53639 Königswinter, Germany

    Recommended by NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Wikipedia

  13. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Bonn

    Brauhaus Bönnsch

    Bonn's own brewpub, pouring the naturally cloudy Bönnsch it has brewed for forty years — the beer is also the name of the Bonn dialect. Rhenish plates, a barrel-vault room and a beer garden by the Sterntor.

    Sterntorbrücke 4, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region, General-Anzeiger Bonn

  14. Must see · Rhenish & German · Bonn

    Em Höttche

    A gasthaus on the market square with a tradition reaching back to 1389 — Bonn's oldest — and the address for uncompromisingly Rhenish cooking: Sauerbraten, Halve Hahn and Reibekuchen. Summer terrace right on the Markt.

    Markt 4, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by General-Anzeiger Bonn, Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region

  15. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Bonn

    halbedel's Gasthaus

    Bonn's flagship gourmet address, a Michelin-starred kitchen in a Wilhelminian villa in Bad Godesberg turning out refined modern French cooking. A star holder for many years running.

    Rheinallee 47, 53173 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

  16. Must see · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Bonn

    Yunico

    A Michelin-starred Japanese fine-dining room on the top floor of the Kameha Grand with sweeping Rhine views, chef Christian Sturm-Willms plating a contemporary omakase and one of Germany's deepest sake lists.

    Am Bonner Bogen 1, 53227 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Der Feinschmecker

  17. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Bonn

    Godesburg

    Dining in the ruins of the Godesburg, in Gottfried Böhm's 1960 building, with a knight's hall, bar and terrace high above Bad Godesberg — German and Mediterranean cooking with a Siebengebirge view.

    Auf dem Godesberg 5, 53177 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Schlemmer Atlas, Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), Wikipedia

  18. Worth the detour · Bakeries, Konditorei & Sweets · Bonn

    Café Profittlich

    A famed traditional Konditorei in a 1731 half-timbered house at the foot of the Drachenfels, run by the Profittlich family since 1892 and known far beyond the region for its Herrentorte and Stollen — a fine stop on the Drachenfels day-trip.

    Drachenfelsstraße 21, 53604 Bad Honnef-Rhöndorf, Germany

    Recommended by Der Feinschmecker, Falstaff, Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region

  19. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Kunstmuseum Bonn

    A leading modern-art museum on the Museumsmeile, holding the finest collection of Rhenish Expressionism — August Macke above all — alongside major postwar German art. Some 9,000 works in a luminous Axel Schultes building.

    Look for Rhenish Expressionism · August Macke

    Helmut-Kohl-Allee 2, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.)

  20. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Deutsches Museum Bonn

    The Bonn outpost of Munich's science museum, at the southern end of the Museumsmeile, showcasing German research and technology since 1945 with plenty of hands-on stations for families.

    Look for Science & technology since 1945

    Ahrstraße 45, 53175 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region

  21. Worth the detour · Bonn

    LVR-LandesMuseum Bonn

    The Rhineland's state museum of archaeology, art and cultural history — 400,000 years in one house, from the original Neanderthal 1 skeleton through Celts and Romans to modern art.

    Look for Neanderthal · Rhineland archaeology

    Colmantstraße 14–16, 53115 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.)

  22. Worth the detour · Bonn

    UN Campus & Langer Eugen

    The heart of Bonn's former government quarter: the 117 m Egon-Eiermann tower 'Langer Eugen', once the Bundestag's office high-rise, now home to a dozen UN organisations. The riverside campus makes Bonn Germany's UN city.

    Look for Former Bundestag tower · UN city

    Platz der Vereinten Nationen 1, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Wikipedia

  23. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Kreuzbergkirche

    A Baroque pilgrimage church above the city whose Heilige Stiege — a Holy Staircase replicating Rome's Scala Santa — was built by the great Balthasar Neumann and consecrated in 1751. One of Bonn's most important monuments.

    Look for Baroque · Balthasar Neumann's Holy Staircase

    Stationsweg 21, 53127 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), baukunst-nrw

  24. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Beethoven-Denkmal

    Germany's oldest Beethoven monument, an 1845 bronze by Ernst Hähnel unveiled for the composer's 75th birthday at the first Beethoven Festival. It presides over the Münsterplatz, the city's favourite square.

    Look for 1845 statue · oldest in Germany

    Münsterplatz, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Wikipedia

  25. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Post Tower

    Helmut Jahn's 162.5 m glass headquarters for DHL/Deutsche Post (2002), the tallest building in Bonn and the defining note of its riverside skyline, its twin elliptical shells split by a full-height atrium.

    Look for Helmut Jahn skyscraper · city's tallest

    Charles-de-Gaulle-Straße 20, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Wikipedia

  26. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Alter Friedhof

    A romantic garden cemetery (from 1715) that is one of Germany's most significant, the resting place of Robert and Clara Schumann, Schiller's wife Charlotte and Beethoven's mother among many university greats. An open-air monument, free to wander.

    Look for Schumann's grave · garden cemetery

    Bornheimer Straße 75, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), Wikipedia

  27. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Museum August Macke Haus

    The home and studio where August Macke lived 1911–14 and painted more than 400 works, now a museum of Rhenish Expressionism with changing shows. Macke staged the landmark 'Rheinische Expressionisten' exhibition here in 1913.

    Look for August Macke's studio-home

    Bornheimer Straße 96, 53119 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.)

  28. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Doppelkirche Schwarzrheindorf

    A rare two-storey Romanesque double church, consecrated in 1151, celebrated for its largely original 12th-century frescoes rediscovered under plaster in 1863. One of the best-known churches in the Rhineland, on the Beuel bank.

    Look for 1151 Romanesque · original frescoes

    Dixstraße 41, 53225 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), baukunst-nrw

  29. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Bonner Rheinuferpromenade

    The city's long Rhine promenade, running from the Beethovenhalle past the Alter Zoll to the UN Campus, with lawns, cafés and constant barge traffic. A newly redesigned stretch makes it Bonn's front porch on the river.

    Look for Rhine promenade walk

    Brassertufer, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region

  30. Worth the detour · Bonn

    Redoute

    A Classicist electoral ballhouse (1790–92) in Bad Godesberg where the young Beethoven played before Joseph Haydn in 1792. Still a grand venue for concerts and receptions, set in the Redoutenpark.

    Look for 1792 ballhouse · Beethoven met Haydn

    Kurfürstenallee 1, 53177 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Wikipedia

  31. Worth the detour · International & Immigrant · Bonn

    Strandhaus

    A beach-house-styled Michelin Guide restaurant in the Altstadt since 2000, doing fresh, seasonal Mediterranean plates in a maritime, laid-back setting.

  33. Worth the detour · International & Immigrant · Bonn

    The Michelin Guide Italian in the AMERON Hotel Königshof, right on the Rhine promenade — polished Italian cooking with river views from the room and terrace.

    Adenauerallee 9, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Der Feinschmecker

  34. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Bonn

    Konrad's

    A Michelin-Plate restaurant and skybar on the 17th floor of the Bonn Marriott, floor-to-ceiling windows over the city, doing modern Mediterranean-leaning cooking.

    Platz der Vereinten Nationen 4, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

  35. Deep cut · Bonn

    Sterntor

    A picturesque city gate rebuilt in 1900 from stones of Bonn's medieval fortification, incorporating a real basalt half-round tower from the old wall. A small window onto how mighty the town's defences once were.

    Look for Reconstructed medieval gate

    Vivatsgasse, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital)

  36. Deep cut · Bonn

    Arithmeum

    A university museum of 'calculating in olden and modern times', holding the world's most comprehensive collection of mechanical calculating machines — from 3,000-year-old clay tokens to modern chips — shown with unusual aesthetic flair.

    Look for Calculating machines

    Lennéstraße 2, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Wikipedia

  37. Deep cut · Bonn

    Frauenmuseum

    Founded in 1981, the world's first museum of women's art and history, with 700-plus exhibitions to its name and an internationally recognised programme. A Bonn original.

    Look for World's first women's museum

    Im Krausfeld 10, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Wikipedia

  38. Deep cut · Bonn

    Namen-Jesu-Kirche

    A former Jesuit church (1686–1717) a few steps from the Beethoven-Haus, a fine example of Rhenish Jesuit Baroque with Romanesque and Gothic touches, today seat of the Old Catholic bishop.

    Look for Jesuit Baroque church

    Bonngasse 8, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), baukunst-nrw

  39. Deep cut · Bonn

    Kanzlerbungalow & Palais Schaumburg

    The heart of the 'Bonn Republic': Palais Schaumburg, chancellery from 1949, and the Sep-Ruf-designed Kanzlerbungalow (1963–64) that was the chancellors' residence and reception house until 1999. On the Weg der Demokratie; visits by prior registration.

    Look for Bonn Republic · chancellor's bungalow

    Adenauerallee 139, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region

  40. Deep cut · Bonn

    Villa Hammerschmidt

    The 'white villa on the Rhine', official seat of the Federal President from 1950 and still his Bonn office. When the President is in residence the standard flies from the roof; occasional guided tours open the state rooms.

    Look for President's Bonn residence

    Adenauerallee 135, 53113 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), Official site of the place

  41. Deep cut · Bonn

    Beethovenhalle

    Bonn's 1959 concert hall by Siegfried Wolske, a listed piece of postwar modernism on the Rhine and long the home of the Beethoven Festival. An iconic city building at the north end of the riverfront.

    Look for 1959 concert hall

    Wachsbleiche 16, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Bonn Tourismus / visit-bonn-region

  42. Deep cut · Bonn

    Stadtpark & Kurpark Bad Godesberg

    Together with the Redoutenpark the spa park forms eight hectares of old trees and lawns, the green centre of former spa-town Bad Godesberg, near the Draitsch mineral spring. A quiet counterpoint to the Godesburg above.

    Look for Spa-town park

    Koblenzer Straße 173, 53177 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bonn (bonn.de), Wikipedia

  43. Deep cut · Rhenish & German · Bonn

    Rheinhotel Dreesen

    The Gobelin restaurant of an 1894 Art-Nouveau grand hotel on the Bad Godesberg riverfront, still run by the founding family — classic German cuisine and one of Bonn's finest Rhine terraces.

    Rheinstraße 45-49, 53179 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Wikipedia

  44. Closed — kept for the record · Michelin & Fine Dining · Bonn

    Kaspars — CLOSED

    The Michelin-starred riverside room of brothers Felix and Lukas Kaspar (star from 2017) closed permanently at year's end, citing chronic gastronomy staff shortages. Listed for the record; no longer operating.

    Rosental 105, 53111 Bonn, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Tageskarte (gastro trade press)

Düsseldorf 74

Altstadt · Kö · MedienHafen · Little Tokyo

  1. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Altstadt & "die längste Theke der Welt"

    Düsseldorf's compact Old Town packs some 260 pubs, brewhouses and bars into less than a square kilometre along the Rhine — the density locals proudly call "the longest bar counter in the world." Bolkerstraße is its spine; it is the city's number-one draw.

    Look for Altstadt

    Bolkerstraße, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Königsallee (die Kö)

    A near-1,000 m luxury boulevard split by a moat-like canal (the former Stadtgraben) and a lime-tree allée, lined with designer boutiques and jewellers. Renamed to honour the king in 1851 after a scandal; at nearly 87 m across it is one of Germany's widest streets.

    Look for Stadtmitte

    Königsallee, 40212 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Neuer Zollhof (Gehry-Bauten) im MedienHafen

    Frank Gehry's ensemble of three leaning, curving towers (1998) — one white-plastered, one red-brick, one mirror-clad stainless steel — is the signature landmark of the redeveloped MedienHafen, a showcase of contemporary architecture beside the old harbour basins.

    Look for MedienHafen

    Neuer Zollhof 1-3, 40221 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  4. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Rheinturm

    At 240.5 m the city's tallest structure (1982), with a 168 m observation deck giving a 360° panorama. Horst Baumann's "Lichtzeitpegel" of 39 portholes in the shaft is recognised by Guinness as the world's largest decimal clock.

    Look for MedienHafen

    Stromstraße 20, 40221 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  5. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Rheinuferpromenade

    After the riverside road was buried in the Rheinufertunnel (1993), Niklaus Fritschi's plane-tree promenade (1990-97) reconnected the Old Town to the Rhine; it won the German Urban Design Prize and is the city's favourite riverside stroll.

    Look for Altstadt

    Mannesmannufer, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, The Düsseldorfer

  6. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Little Tokyo (Immermannstraße)

    Germany's largest Japanese quarter, around Immermann-, Ost- and Klosterstraße near the Hauptbahnhof. Home to roughly 6,500 Japanese residents (Europe's third-largest Japanese community), it is a genuine signature — ramen shops, izakaya, sushi bars, bookshops and supermarkets.

    Look for Stadtmitte

    Immermannstraße, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, SWD

  7. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Basilika St. Lambertus

    The Old Town's mother church, a Lower-Rhenish brick-Gothic hall church consecrated in 1394. Its twisted, "leaning" tower roof — the Schiefer Turm — has defined the Rhine silhouette for centuries and is a city emblem.

    Look for Altstadt

    Stiftsplatz 7, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  8. Must see · Düsseldorf

    K20 – Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen

    The state's flagship modern-art museum behind a curved black-granite façade, holding a classic-modern collection — Klee, Picasso, Warhol, Rauschenberg, Judd, Johns, Stella — and a famous Paul Klee trove.

    Look for Altstadt

    Grabbeplatz 5, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen (official), Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  9. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Museum Kunstpalast

    Rooted in 1902 and set in the monumental 1920s Ehrenhof complex by the Rhine, the Kunstpalast spans old masters to modern art and design across 5,000 m² of galleries, plus a renowned glass collection.

    Look for Pempelfort / Ehrenhof

    Ehrenhof 4-5, 40479 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  10. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Schloss Benrath

    A late-Rococo pleasure palace (1755-73) by Nicolas de Pigage for Elector Karl Theodor, its pink corps de logis set in a 60-hectare park of ponds and canals — architecture, garden and interiors conceived as one Gesamtkunstwerk.

    Look for Benrath

    Benrather Schloßallee 100-106, 40597 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  11. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Kaiserpfalz Kaiserswerth

    The mighty riverside ruin of Emperor Friedrich Barbarossa's imperial palace, expanded 1174-84 on a stronghold first documented in 1016. Restored 1997-2002 and open to walk through, it anchors the pretty Kaiserswerth quarter.

    Look for Kaiserswerth

    Burgallee, 40489 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by NRW-Stiftung, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  12. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Hofgarten

    Germany's first and oldest public park (Volksgarten), begun 1769 under Nicolas de Pigage; a 27-hectare "green island" of lawns, monuments and sculpture running from Schloss Jägerhof to the Rhine terraces.

    Look for Pempelfort

    Hofgartenstraße, 40479 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  13. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Carlsplatz Markt

    Düsseldorf's oldest surviving daily market, at the Old Town's edge: 60-plus covered stalls of fruit, cheese, fish, flowers and regional produce, plus warm street food, open Monday to Saturday.

    Look for Carlstadt

    Carlsplatz, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, SWD

  14. Must see · Düsseldorf

    Kö-Bogen II

    Ingenhoven's five-storey retail-and-office building (2020) wraps 8 km of hornbeam hedge — over 30,000 plants — across roof and slanted façades, billed as Europe's largest green façade, framing the redesigned Gustaf-Gründgens-Platz.

    Look for Stadtmitte

    Schadowstraße 50-52, 40212 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Westdeutsche Zeitung

  15. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Düsseldorf

    Uerige

    The archetypal Düsseldorf brewhouse, brewing dark, hoppy-bitter Altbier in the Old Town since 1862 — regularly voted among Germany's best beers, poured from the wood by Köbes and drunk standing at the copper counter. Its twice-yearly Sticke is a cult event.

    Berger Straße 1, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Official site of the place

  16. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Düsseldorf

    Brauerei im Füchschen

    A boisterous house brewery on Ratinger Straße pouring Füchschen Alt (brewed here since 1848) alongside hearty Rhenish plates — the roast Schweinshaxe is the classic order. A carnival institution.

    Ratinger Straße 28, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  17. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Düsseldorf

    Brauerei Schumacher / Stammhaus

    Founded 1838, the oldest of the city's house breweries and cradle of Düsseldorf Altbier: Schumacher Alt has been brewed to family recipe for over 175 years, served with Rhenish cooking on Oststraße and at the Old-Town Stammhaus "Im goldenen Kessel."

    Oststraße 123, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Time Out, Wikipedia

  18. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Düsseldorf

    Hausbrauerei Zum Schlüssel

    A big, convivial Bolkerstraße brewhouse pouring full-bodied Schlüssel Alt (brewed on-site since 1850, a European Beer Star gold winner) with classic brauhaus fare in the thick of the "longest bar."

    Bolkerstraße 41-47, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  19. Must see · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Takumi

    Little Tokyo's most famous ramen house, in Sapporo style — broths simmered up to eight hours, red-miso, shoyu and tonkotsu bowls plus tantanmen. So popular it has spun off several nearby siblings.

    Immermannstraße 28, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Mit Vergnügen, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  20. Must see · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Naniwa

    Open in Little Tokyo since 1986 and still the reference for ramen — house-made noodles in robust shio, shoyu and miso broths, plus gyoza and yakisoba. The daily queue is part of the ritual.

    Oststraße 55, 40211 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Japan Digest, Mr. Düsseldorf

  21. Must see · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Nagaya

    Yoshizumi Nagaya's Little-Tokyo flagship — the only Japanese restaurant in Germany to hold a Michelin star continuously since 2012, blending classical Japanese technique with subtle Western notes.

    Klosterstraße 42, 40211 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  22. Must see · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Yoshi by Nagaya

    Nagaya's second Michelin-starred house (a star since 2017), given over to kaiseki: an evening omakase of eight ingredient-led courses of exacting precision. It makes Nagaya Germany's only two-star Japanese chef.

    Kreuzstraße 17, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  23. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Düsseldorf

    Agata's

    A Michelin-starred Unterbilk restaurant praised for "cuisine full of finesse" — creative cooking with international influences, one of the city's most consistent fine-dining addresses.

    Kirchfeldstraße 59, 40217 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

  24. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Düsseldorf

    LA VIE by Thomas Bühner

    Star chef Thomas Bühner's return, opened May 2025 in Flingern and awarded a Michelin star just 46 days later — an elegant marriage of French and Asian cooking, with a rotating vegan menu.

    Schlüterstraße 1, 40235 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  25. Must see · Bakeries, Konditorei & Sweets · Düsseldorf

    Konditorei Heinemann

    A confectionery renowned far beyond the city for its Champagnertrüffel — handmade since 1968 with Épernay Champagne — plus café-patisserie counters around the Kö. A Düsseldorf sweet institution.

    Bahnstraße 16, 40212 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Königsallee Düsseldorf (official boulevard site), Official site of the place

  26. Must see · Bakeries, Konditorei & Sweets · Düsseldorf

    Bäckerei Josef Hinkel

    A fourth-generation Old-Town bakery (since 1891) beloved as "die Bäckerei der Brotfreunde," working exclusively with natural sourdoughs and craft methods. Listed by the Deutsches Brotinstitut and Der Feinschmecker.

    Hohe Straße 31, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Deutsches Brotinstitut, Der Feinschmecker

  27. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    St. Andreas

    The former court and Jesuit church (1622-29), a key monument of the late Renaissance-into-Baroque, holding the electoral Wittelsbach mausoleum. Cared for by the Dominicans since 1972.

    Look for Altstadt

    Andreasstraße 27, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Förderverein Romanische Kirchen Köln, Wikipedia

  28. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    K21 – Kunstsammlung im Ständehaus

    The Kunstsammlung's home for art since 1980, in the domed former Rhenish parliament (Ständehaus). Best known for Tomás Saraceno's walk-on wire installation "in orbit" suspended beneath the glass roof.

    Look for Unterbilk

    Ständehausstraße 1, 40217 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen (official), Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  29. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    NRW-Forum

    An exhibition house in the Ehrenhof devoted to photography, pop and digital culture, with festivals, workshops and boundary-pushing shows for a broad audience.

    Look for Pempelfort / Ehrenhof

    Ehrenhof 2, 40479 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  30. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    EKŌ-Haus der japanischen Kultur

    A Japanese cultural centre (1993) in Niederkassel with Germany's largest Buddhist temple, traditional gardens, a tea house and tea ceremonies — the contemplative counterpart to Little Tokyo across the river.

    Look for Niederkassel

    Brüggener Weg 6, 40547 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  31. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Japanischer Garten im Nordpark

    A gift of Düsseldorf's Japanese community since 1975, tucked in the quiet north-west corner of Nordpark: a waterfall, island pond, azaleas and Japanese maples laid out to traditional symbolism. Free and open around the clock.

    Look for Stockum / Nordpark

    Kaiserswerther Straße 365, 40474 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  32. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    SchifffahrtMuseum im Schlossturm

    The round Schlossturm on Burgplatz is the sole survivor of the ducal castle (burned in the 19th century). Since 1984 it houses Germany's oldest inland-navigation museum, telling 2,000 years of Rhine shipping.

    Look for Altstadt

    Burgplatz 30, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Musenkuss Düsseldorf (city cultural portal)

  33. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Hetjens – Deutsches Keramikmuseum

    Germany's only museum devoted entirely to ceramics, in the Baroque Palais Nesselrode, with exhibits up to 8,000 years old spanning the whole world of pottery and porcelain.

    Look for Carlstadt

    Schulstraße 4, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  34. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Heinrich-Heine-Institut

    In patrician houses on Bilker Straße, the world's only Heine museum plus archive and library — a centre of international research on the great poet born in Düsseldorf in 1797.

    Look for Carlstadt

    Bilker Straße 12-14, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Musenkuss Düsseldorf (city cultural portal)

  35. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Aquazoo Löbbecke Museum

    A combined aquarium, zoo and natural-history museum (1987) on the edge of Nordpark, showing about 500 species across 25 themed rooms with aquariums, terrariums and a tropical hall.

    Look for Stockum / Nordpark

    Kaiserswerther Straße 380, 40474 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  36. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Kiefernstraße (Flingern) Street Art

    A former squatters' street now painted end to end — the city's largest continuous artwork and an open-air gallery of murals by local and international artists, at the heart of buzzy, creative Flingern.

    Look for Flingern

    Kiefernstraße, 40233 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, SWD

  37. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    KIT – Kunst im Tunnel

    A contemporary-art space (opened 2007) in a light-filled vault set between the road tunnels beneath the Rhine promenade, showing emerging artists — with a café on the riverbank above.

    Look for Altstadt

    Mannesmannufer 1b, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  38. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Tonhalle Düsseldorf

    Wilhelm Kreis's domed 1926 planetarium at the Ehrenhof, converted to a concert hall in 1976-78. Its 38 m blue dome, now studded with LEDs for an "indoor starry sky," hosts around 300 concerts a year.

    Look for Pempelfort / Ehrenhof

    Ehrenhof 1, 40479 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Westdeutsche Zeitung

  39. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Botanischer Garten der HHU (Kuppelgewächshaus)

    The university's botanical garden in Bilk, whose landmark 18 m filigree dome greenhouse — a Mediterranean "cold house" of some 400 species from Australia to California — is a much-loved free retreat.

    Look for Bilk

    Universitätsstraße 1, 40225 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Wikipedia

  40. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Dreischeibenhaus & Schauspielhaus

    An icon duo on Gustaf-Gründgens-Platz: HPP's 94 m glass "three-slice" tower (1957-60) and Bernhard Pfau's flowing white theatre (1970), postwar-modern landmarks now framed by the green Kö-Bogen II.

    Look for Stadtmitte

    Gustaf-Gründgens-Platz 1, 40211 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  41. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Landtag Nordrhein-Westfalen

    The state parliament (1988), the first purpose-built Landtag in postwar West Germany: an all-circles composition of round plenary and committee halls facing the Rhine. Free visits by prior registration.

    Look for MedienHafen

    Platz des Landtags 1, 40221 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  42. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Jan-Wellem-Reiterdenkmal & Marktplatz

    Gabriel de Grupello's Baroque equestrian statue (1711) of art-loving Elector Johann Wilhelm II stands before the Renaissance-and-later town hall on the Old Town's Marktplatz — a favourite meeting point.

    Look for Altstadt

    Marktplatz, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, baukunst-nrw

  43. Worth the detour · Düsseldorf

    Kunsthalle Düsseldorf

    A rare Brutalist landmark on Grabbeplatz — a 1967 concrete cube on black basalt — showing changing contemporary exhibitions without a permanent collection; listed as a monument in 2024.

    Look for Altstadt

    Grabbeplatz 4, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  44. Worth the detour · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Düsseldorf

    Frankenheim Brauereiausschank

    The tavern of the Frankenheim private brewery (founded 1873), pouring its top-fermented Alt in great quantity across three big rooms and a beer garden, with rustic Rhenish specialities.

    Wielandstraße 12-14, 40211 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Mr. Düsseldorf

  45. Worth the detour · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Düsseldorf

    Brauerei zur Uel

    A historic Ratinger-Straße brauhaus with 18th-century roots, named for its owl-filled rooms (Uel = Eule), serving gutbürgerliche Rhenish plates and Füchschen Alt in the Old Town's liveliest pub row.

    Ratinger Straße 16, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  46. Worth the detour · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Maruyasu

    A family-run, self-service Japanese diner on Immermannstraße: pick sushi, bento, tempura and udon from the case and settle at the counter. Founder Akio Ando helped introduce raw fish to the city in 1995.

    Immermannstraße 11, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Bento Daisuki

  47. Worth the detour · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Yabase

    An unadorned, deeply authentic Little-Tokyo Japanese where much of the room is Japanese business diners — widely rated the city's best sushi, with very fresh, precise nigiri and sashimi. Reservations essential.

    Klosterstraße 70, 40211 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Mr. Düsseldorf, Prinz Düsseldorf

  48. Worth the detour · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Kushi-Tei of Tokyo

    An authentic izakaya whose speciality is yakitori grilled over real charcoal, as in Tokyo's backstreets, alongside sushi cut by the master — a Little-Tokyo all-rounder.

    Immermannstraße 38, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Falstaff, Mr. Düsseldorf

  49. Worth the detour · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Soba-An

    A rarity: a dedicated soba house on Klosterstraße where Tamaki Hamano — reputedly Germany's only female soba master — makes buckwheat noodles by hand at an open counter.

    Klosterstraße 68, 40211 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Verliebt in Japan

  50. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Düsseldorf

    1876 Daniel Dal-Ben

    A tiny 14-seat Michelin-starred room in Düsseltal where Daniel Dal-Ben cooks a creative set menu drawing on French, Italian and Japanese influences — one of the city's hardest tables to book.

    Grunerstraße 42a, 40239 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Mr. Düsseldorf

  51. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Düsseldorf

    Fritz's Frau Franzi

    The Michelin-starred restaurant of the boutique Fritz Hotel near the Kö, an "experimental world kitchen" of creative, locally sourced small plates that shift with the season.

    Adersstraße 8, 40215 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Time Out

  52. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Düsseldorf

    Le Flair

    A Michelin-starred French restaurant in Pempelfort (a star since 2017), purist and product-driven, with a flexible menu that stresses taste quality and respect for its ingredients.

    Marc-Chagall-Straße 108, 40477 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Westdeutsche Zeitung

  53. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Düsseldorf

    Setzkasten

    A one-of-a-kind Michelin-starred concept by chef Egor Hopp in the basement of the Zurheide Feine Kost gourmet supermarket near the Kö — fine dining wrapped around one of Germany's great food halls.

    Berliner Allee 52, 40212 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Tageskarte (gastro trade press)

  54. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Düsseldorf

    Im Schiffchen

    Jean-Claude Bourgueil's Michelin-starred temple of classic cuisine in a Baroque brick house on Kaiserswerther Markt — once a three-star great, still a benchmark of refined, produce-led cooking.

    Kaiserswerther Markt 9, 40489 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

  55. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Düsseldorf

    Münstermanns Kontor

    A Carlstadt institution grown from the Münstermann family delicatessen: a lively open-kitchen bistro with a daily-changing card of European classics from bouillabaisse to Wiener Schnitzel. In the Michelin guide.

    Hohe Straße 11, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf

  56. Worth the detour · Vegan & Vegetarian · Düsseldorf

    Sattgrün (Medienhafen)

    A much-loved all-vegan buffet — warm dishes, salads, soups, seitan and cakes, priced by plate size — with several Düsseldorf branches, this one in the MedienHafen.

    Brückenstraße 12, 40221 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Mr. Düsseldorf, Deutschland is(s)t vegan

  57. Worth the detour · Coffee & Café · Düsseldorf

    Kaffeehandwerk

    A pioneering third-wave roastery-café in Flingern, roasting its own beans and pulling carefully sourced filter and espresso — a fixture of the city's specialty-coffee scene.

    Birkenstraße 127, 40233 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Crema Magazin (coffee), Mr. Düsseldorf

  58. Deep cut · Düsseldorf

    Stadterhebungsmonument

    Bert Gerresheim's dense bronze tableau (1988) near Burgplatz marks the city's 700th anniversary, depicting the Battle of Worringen that won Düsseldorf its town charter in 1288.

    Look for Altstadt

    Joseph-Wimmer-Gasse, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Wikipedia

  59. Deep cut · Düsseldorf

    Bilker Bunker

    A 1942 high-rise air-raid bunker, listed since 2014 and reopened in 2023 as an art-and-culture house: rotating exhibitions, performances and the club Schleuse Zwei — concrete meets Bilk's creative scene.

    Look for Bilk

    Aachener Straße 39, 40223 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, baukunst-nrw

  60. Deep cut · Düsseldorf

    Roncalli's Apollo Varieté

    A 500-seat variety theatre (1997) slotted as a glass box beneath the Rheinkniebrücke beside the Landtag, run in the Roncalli tradition — acrobatics, music and cabaret by the river.

    Look for Altstadt / Rheinufer

    Apollo-Platz 1, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Wikipedia

  61. Deep cut · Düsseldorf

    Alt St. Martin (Bilk)

    Düsseldorf's oldest surviving building: a small tufa church in Bilk whose origins reach back to around 700, with an 12th-century five-storey tower. Once the parish church for the whole settlement.

    Look for Bilk

    Martinstraße 72, 40223 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia, baukunst-nrw

  62. Deep cut · Düsseldorf

    Filmmuseum & Black Box Kino

    The city's film museum in Carlstadt traces the whole history of cinema; its Black Box arthouse cinema (133 seats, with a historic cinema organ for silent films) screens repertory and festival programmes.

    Look for Carlstadt

    Schulstraße 4, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Musenkuss Düsseldorf (city cultural portal)

  63. Deep cut · Düsseldorf

    St. Rochus (Rochuskirche)

    A striking modern church (1953-55) by Paul Schneider-Esleben: a triple-shell, egg-shaped concrete dome — symbol of resurrection — grafted onto the surviving old tower, with fittings by sculptor Ewald Mataré.

    Look for Pempelfort

    Rochusmarkt 5, 40479 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Wikipedia

  64. Deep cut · Düsseldorf

    Wilhelm-Marx-Haus

    Wilhelm Kreis's 57 m brick tower (1922-24) was Germany's first high-rise and briefly the tallest reinforced-concrete building in Europe. A protected monument at the edge of the Old Town.

    Look for Stadtmitte

    Heinrich-Heine-Allee 53, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Westdeutsche Zeitung

  65. Deep cut · Düsseldorf

    Südpark

    At 70 hectares the city's largest and most-visited park, created for the 1987 Bundesgartenschau around the older Volksgarten; three contrasting garden landscapes plus one of the world's largest climbing-net structures.

    Look for Bilk / Wersten

    Am Südpark, 40225 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Westdeutsche Zeitung, Wikipedia

  66. Deep cut · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Düsseldorf

    Brauhaus Joh. Albrecht

    A listed brewhouse on the left bank in Niederkassel, brewing and cooking in a former Kornbrennerei building for nearly 30 years — its own rotating beers with hearty German fare.

    Niederkasseler Straße 104, 40547 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Schlemmer Atlas, Prinz Düsseldorf

  67. Deep cut · Japanese & Little Tokyo · Düsseldorf

    Takezo Ramen Bar

    A compact Immermannstraße ramen bar near the station serving the full range from shoyu to tantanmen — a reliable Little-Tokyo noodle stop.

    Immermannstraße 48, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Bento Daisuki

  68. Deep cut · Bakeries, Konditorei & Sweets · Düsseldorf

    Bing Go

    A little Immermannstraße sweet spot for taiyaki — fish-shaped cakes filled with classic anko or creative fillings — a favourite Little-Tokyo snack since 2020.

    Immermannstraße 27, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Düsseldorf Tourismus / visitduesseldorf, Mr. Düsseldorf

  69. Deep cut · International & Immigrant · Düsseldorf

    Enzo im Schiffchen

    The young, more casual ground-floor restaurant of the Im Schiffchen house in Kaiserswerth, awarded a Michelin star of its own for Bourgueil's creative Italian-Mediterranean cooking.

    Kaiserswerther Markt 9, 40489 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

  70. Deep cut · International & Immigrant · Düsseldorf

    Meerbar

    A seafood restaurant-and-bar in the red Gehry building of the MedienHafen — Mediterranean-French cooking around daily-fresh fish (its "Sexy Fish" theme), with a long bar and lounge for after.

    Neuer Zollhof 1, 40221 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Schlemmer Atlas, Prinz Düsseldorf

  71. Deep cut · International & Immigrant · Düsseldorf

    Phox

    A modern Vietnamese kitchen focused on pho, named by Der Feinschmecker among Germany's ten best Vietnamese restaurants — a strong immigrant-cuisine pick near Little Tokyo.

    Stresemannstraße 32, 40210 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Der Feinschmecker, The Dorf (Düsseldorf lifestyle magazine)

  72. Deep cut · Coffee & Café · Düsseldorf

    Lightroast

    A micro-roastery and café in Flingern, opening its backyard works for espresso and beans — a small, serious address for specialty coffee.

    Hoffeldstraße 104, 40235 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by The Dorf (Düsseldorf lifestyle magazine), Mr. Düsseldorf

  73. Deep cut · Coffee & Café · Düsseldorf

    Café Hüftgold

    A cosy Flingern café that has baked lovingly homemade cakes for over 20 years — "Genuss ohne Reue" — and become a neighbourhood status symbol on Ackerstraße, anchoring the quarter's street-art strip.

    Ackerstraße 113, 40233 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Rheintopf (Rhineland food magazine), Life in Düsseldorf

  74. Closed — kept for the record · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · Düsseldorf

    Brauerei zum Schiffchen — CLOSED

    Düsseldorf's oldest restaurant (established 1628, where Napoleon dined in 1811) and a byword for original Old-Town dining. CLOSED since autumn 2024 pending renovation; kept here as heritage, not a live tip.

    Hafenstraße 5, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia, The Düsseldorfer

The Rhine Corridor 45

Brühl · Bergisch Gladbach · Leverkusen · Neuss · Zons

  1. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Schlösser Augustusburg & Falkenlust (UNESCO-Welterbe)

    Two early-Rococo masterpieces in Brühl — the sumptuous residence Augustusburg with Balthasar Neumann's grand ceremonial staircase, and the intimate hunting lodge Falkenlust — set in a formal French garden. Together with the garden they have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984, the corridor's cultural crown.

    Look for Rococo palaces · UNESCO since 1984

    Schlossstraße 6, 50321 Brühl, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Stadt Brühl Tourismus

  2. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Max Ernst Museum Brühl des LVR

    The world's only museum devoted to the whole life and work of Dadaist and Surrealist Max Ernst, born in Brühl in 1891. A neoclassical villa with a glass extension holds sculptures, graphics and the 36 intimate 'D-paintings' Ernst gave his wife Dorothea Tanning.

    Look for Only Max Ernst museum worldwide

    Comesstraße 42 / Max-Ernst-Allee 1, 50321 Brühl, Germany

    Recommended by Landschaftsverband Rheinland (LVR), Stadt Brühl Tourismus, NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.)

  3. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Museum Insel Hombroich

    A singular 'art parallel to nature' on 25 hectares of Erft meadowland near Neuss: walk-in pavilions holding works from Cézanne and Rembrandt to Asian antiquities, set loose in a wild landscape with no labels and one flat entry fee. Includes the Kirkeby-Feld and the former NATO Raketenstation.

    Look for Art island in the meadows

    Minkel 2, 41472 Neuss, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, RadRegionRheinland / Region Köln-Bonn, NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.)

  4. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Langen Foundation

    Tadao Ando's serene concrete-and-glass museum (2004) on the former Hombroich missile base, a long glazed hall crossed by two half-buried concrete wings. It shows the Viktor and Marianne Langen collection of Japanese and modern art in changing exhibitions.

    Look for Tadao Ando art house on the Raketenstation

    Raketenstation Hombroich 1, 41472 Neuss, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Düsseldorf Tourismus (visitduesseldorf.de), Wikipedia

  5. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Quirinus-Münster Neuss

    A three-aisled vaulted galleried basilica (1209–1230), one of the great late-Romanesque churches of the Lower Rhine, crowned by a Baroque lantern dome. It holds the relics of St Quirinus, the city's patron, and was raised to a Basilica minor by Benedict XVI in 2009.

    Look for Late-Romanesque basilica · St Quirinus

    Münsterplatz 23, 41460 Neuss, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Stadt Neuss (neuss.de), Wikipedia

  6. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Japanischer Garten Leverkusen

    A jewel-like Japanese garden begun in 1912 by Bayer director Carl Duisberg and reshaped after his 1926 trip to Japan, with ponds, arched bridges, lanterns and maples. Set inside the Carl-Duisberg-Park on the Bayer Chempark, free and open year-round.

    Look for 1912 Japanese garden · free

    Kaiser-Wilhelm-Allee, 51373 Leverkusen, Germany

    Recommended by Bayer AG (bayer.com), Stadt Leverkusen (leverkusen.de), baukunst-nrw

  7. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Schloss Bensberg

    One of Germany's largest Baroque palaces, a hilltop hunting seat begun for Elector Johann Wilhelm in the early 1700s, with sweeping views over Cologne and the Rhine plain. Long a cadet school, since 2000 the Althoff Grandhotel — home to the 2-star Vendôme.

    Look for Baroque hilltop palace · grand hotel

    Kadettenstraße 1, 51429 Bergisch Gladbach, Germany

    Recommended by NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Das Bergische (Naturarena Bergisches Land), Wikipedia

  8. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Abtei Brauweiler

    A former Benedictine abbey founded in 1024 by the Palatine count Ezzo and his wife Mathilde, its great Romanesque church begun in 1135 and a four-winged Baroque cloister added from 1780. Now the LVR cultural centre, marking its 1,000-year jubilee.

    Look for 1024 Benedictine abbey · Romanesque church

    Ehrenfriedstraße 19, 50259 Pulheim, Germany

    Recommended by Landschaftsverband Rheinland (LVR), baukunst-nrw, Rhein-Erft Tourismus

  9. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Kloster Knechtsteden

    A former Premonstratensian abbey founded around 1130, its double-choir Romanesque basilica (1138–1181) preserving a rare 12th-century apse fresco of Christ in Majesty. One of the oldest pilgrimage sites in the Rhineland, run by the Spiritans since 1896.

    Look for 12th-c. Romanesque basilica · original fresco

    Knechtsteden 4, 41540 Dormagen, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Stadt Dormagen (dormagen.de)

  10. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Zollfeste Zons

    A remarkably complete medieval customs fortress on the Rhine, laid out from 1372 when the Cologne archbishop moved his toll here, with towers, gates and walls still ringing the little town. The mighty Rheinturm of 1388 and the Judde and Mühlenturm are the picture-book sights.

    Look for Intact medieval Rhine customs town

    Schloßstraße 2–4, 41541 Dormagen, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Dormagen (dormagen.de), Niederrhein Tourismus, Westdeutsche Zeitung

  11. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Abtei Michaelsberg

    A Benedictine abbey founded on the Michaelsberg by Cologne's Archbishop Anno II in 1064, its baroque bulk crowning Siegburg's skyline. Rebuilt after wartime destruction and, since 2017, a spiritual conference centre — the town's near-1,000-year landmark.

    Look for 1064 hilltop Benedictine abbey

    Bergstraße 26, 53721 Siegburg, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Stadt Siegburg / Tourismus Siegburg

  12. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Schloss Dyck

    One of the Rhineland's most important moated castles, spread over four islands in the Kelzenberger Bach and wrapped in a 70-hectare early-19th-century English landscape park with rare ancient trees. Now an international centre for garden art.

    Look for Moated castle · English landscape park

    Schloss-Dyck-Straße 1, 41363 Jüchen, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Deutsche Stiftung Denkmalschutz

  13. Must see · Kölsch, Altbier & Brauhaus · The Rhine Corridor

    Brauhaus Im Dom

    Neuss's oldest inn and only surviving house brewery, brewing on this spot documented since 1607. Beside Bolten it is one of the world's oldest Altbier breweries — pour a Dom's Alt with hearty seasonal Rhenish plates in a medieval building by the Münster.

    Michaelstraße 75–77, 41460 Neuss, Germany

    Recommended by Westdeutsche Zeitung, KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Stadt Neuss (neuss.de)

  14. Must see · The Rhine Corridor

    Klosterruine Heisterbach

    The romantic ruin of a Cistercian abbey founded in 1192 in a wooded Siebengebirge valley; only the soaring choir apse of its once-vast church survives, a favourite of the Rhine Romantics, set in a landscaped park. Free to wander.

    Look for Cistercian choir ruin in the Siebengebirge

    Heisterbacher Straße, 53639 Königswinter, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital), Wikipedia

  15. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · The Rhine Corridor

    Restaurant Vendôme

    The corridor's gastronomic summit, in the Althoff Grandhotel Schloss Bensberg: Joachim Wissler held three Michelin stars here for 17 years (two since 2022) before handing the kitchen to sous-chef Dennis Kuckuck in October 2025. Classic French base, modern signatures, and a strong vegetarian menu.

    Kadettenstraße 1, 51429 Bergisch Gladbach, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Bürgerportal Bergisch Gladbach (in-gl.de)

  16. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · The Rhine Corridor

    Schote by Nelson Müller

    TV chef Nelson Müller moved his Essen restaurant into the new Diepeschrather Mühle in a forest clearing in January 2025; after a year without a star it regained a Michelin star in the 2026 guide. Sustainable, ambitious cooking at a 30-seat chef's-table room with an open kitchen.

    Diepeschrather Weg 80A, 51469 Bergisch Gladbach, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Bürgerportal Bergisch Gladbach (in-gl.de)

  17. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · The Rhine Corridor

    Anthony's Kitchen

    Ghanaian-born, Wiesbaden-raised chef Anthony Sarpong has held a Michelin star in Meerbusch since 2015, blending West African flavours with modern European technique. One of the few starred kitchens between Cologne and Düsseldorf.

    Moerser Straße 81, 40667 Meerbusch, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

  18. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Phantasialand

    One of Germany's best and most-visited theme parks, drawing over two million guests a year to seven immersive themed worlds — Berlin, China, Mexico, Deep in Africa, Fantasy, Mystery and the acclaimed new Klugheim and Rookburgh — with some of Europe's most admired roller coasters.

    Look for Top German theme park · 7 themed worlds

    Berggeiststraße 31–41, 50321 Brühl, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, RadRegionRheinland / Region Köln-Bonn, Stadt Brühl Tourismus

  19. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Skulpturenhalle Thomas Schütte

    An elliptical, column-free exhibition hall built to a model by Golden-Lion sculptor Thomas Schütte and opened in 2016, set among the Hombroich cultural grounds between the Museum Insel and the Langen Foundation. It shows Schütte's own work and changing sculpture exhibitions.

    Look for Thomas Schütte's sculpture hall

    Lindenweg / Ecke Berger Weg, 41472 Neuss-Holzheim, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Baukultur Nordrhein-Westfalen, Rheinische Art (Kunstmagazin)

  20. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Clemens-Sels-Museum & Novaesium

    Neuss's municipal museum — Rhenish Late Gothic, Symbolism and 20th-century art — alongside the restored Roman collection from Novaesium, the oldest Roman military site on the Lower Rhine, where legions were stationed from the 1st century AD.

    Look for Roman Novaesium · Rhenish art

    Am Obertor, 41460 Neuss, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Stadt Neuss (neuss.de), KuLaDig (LVR Kultur.Landschaft.Digital)

  21. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Museum Morsbroich

    Leverkusen's museum of modern and contemporary art, in a Baroque moated palace (Schloss Morsbroich) with a mirror hall and a sculpture park. Founded 1951 as one of the first postwar contemporary-art museums in Germany.

    Look for Modern art in a Baroque Schloss

    Gustav-Heinemann-Straße 80, 51377 Leverkusen, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Stadt Leverkusen (leverkusen.de), baukunst-nrw

  22. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    BayArena

    The compact, atmospheric home of Bundesliga club Bayer 04 Leverkusen — the 2024 German champions — seating about 30,000 in the heart of the city, with a hotel built into the stand and stadium tours on non-match days.

    Look for Bayer 04's Bundesliga stadium

    Bismarckstraße 122–124, 51373 Leverkusen, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, RadRegionRheinland / Region Köln-Bonn, Stadt Leverkusen (leverkusen.de)

  23. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Neuland-Park

    A 25-hectare park on the Rhine, laid out for the 2005 Landesgartenschau on a capped former landfill, that reconnected Leverkusen's centre to the river. Flowering slopes, play areas and long riverside paths.

    Look for Rhine park on a reclaimed Landesgartenschau site

    Nobelstraße 91, 51373 Leverkusen, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, European Garden Heritage Network, Wikipedia

  24. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Kunstmuseum Villa Zanders

    The art museum of Bergisch Gladbach in the grand villa of the Zanders paper dynasty, with about 1,500 m² over three floors devoted to contemporary art and a celebrated collection of art made from and with paper.

    Look for Contemporary & paper art in a paper-baron's villa

    Konrad-Adenauer-Platz 8, 51465 Bergisch Gladbach, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, Das Bergische (Naturarena Bergisches Land), Naturpark Bergisches Land

  25. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Insel Grafenwerth

    A car-free Rhine island reached on foot from Bad Honnef, laid out as a 15-hectare park with lawns, a beer garden, an open-air pool and mini-golf, and a superb view onto the silhouette of the Siebengebirge. The town's riverside playground for a century.

    Look for Car-free Rhine island park

    Lohfelder Straße 7, 53604 Bad Honnef, Germany

    Recommended by Bad Honnef Tourismus (meinbadhonnef.de), Bonn Tourismus (visit-bonn-region.de), Wikipedia

  26. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Schloss Paffendorf

    A romantic moated Renaissance castle (1531–1546), remodelled in neo-Gothic style in the 19th century, on a triangular island in a landscape park. Home to RWE Power's information centre on the Rhenish lignite region, with a café and free garden.

    Look for Moated Renaissance castle · park

    Burggasse, 50126 Bergheim, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bergheim (city.bergheim.de), baukunst-nrw, Rhein-Erft Tourismus

  27. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Schloss Bedburg

    A moated castle whose brick core is among the oldest in the Rhineland, rebuilt as a Renaissance palace after 1588 and later home to the Rhenish Knights' Academy. It stands in the centre of Bedburg on the Mühlenerft, a venue for concerts and events.

    Look for Early brick castle · Renaissance palace

    Graf-Salm-Straße 34, 50181 Bedburg, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Bedburg (bedburg.de), Rhein-Erft Tourismus, Wikipedia

  28. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Museum Keramion

    An internationally renowned ceramics museum in Frechen — long a stoneware town famed for its 'Bartmann' jugs — founded 1971 by stoneware magnate Gottfried Cremer. Peter Neufert's landmark building is a glazed rotunda shaped like a giant potter's wheel.

    Look for Ceramics in a potter's-wheel rotunda

    Bonnstraße 12, 50226 Frechen, Germany

    Recommended by Official site of the place, NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Rhein-Erft Tourismus

  29. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Glasmuseum Rheinbach

    Rheinbach's glass museum, in the historic Himmeroder Hof, tells the story of the 'glass town' shaped after 1947 by expelled Bohemian glass refiners. Baroque to Art Nouveau glass and studio glass since the 1960s.

    Look for Glass town · Bohemian & studio glass

    Himmeroder Wall 6, 53359 Rheinbach, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Rheinbach (rheinbach.de), NRW Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Wikipedia

  30. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · The Rhine Corridor

    Brühler Wirtshaus am Schloss

    In Brühl's restored 1844 station beside the UNESCO palace park, a Rhenish wirtshaus for the classics — Himmel un Äd with Flönz, Halve Hahn, Flammkuchen and grills — with a Kölsch in the castle-park beer garden and a view to Augustusburg.

    Max-Ernst-Allee 2, 50321 Brühl, Germany

    Recommended by koeln.de (Stadtportal), Falstaff, Stadt Brühl Tourismus

  31. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Siebengebirge — Großer Ölberg

    The 461 m Großer Ölberg is the highest summit of the Siebengebirge, Germany's oldest nature reserve, reached by forest trails from Margarethenhöhe or Königswinter. Its summit terrace opens far-reaching views over the range toward the Eifel — the corridor's great hiking country above the Rhine.

    Look for Highest Siebengebirge summit · oldest German reserve

    Großer Ölberg, 53639 Königswinter, Germany

    Recommended by Mit Vergnügen, Wikipedia

  32. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Petersberg

    A Siebengebirge summit above the Rhine crowned by a pilgrimage chapel and the grand hotel that served as the Federal Republic's official guest house — seat of the Allied High Commission after 1945 and host to Kennedy, Gorbachev and the 1999 Petersberg talks. Sweeping river and range views.

    Look for Bundesgästehaus summit · Rhine panorama

    Petersberg, 53639 Königswinter, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Official site of the place

  33. Worth the detour · The Rhine Corridor

    Bilderbuchmuseum Burg Wissem

    Housed in the manor house of Burg Wissem, Europe's museum for the art of the picture book, with a high-quality collection of original illustration and lively shows for families. Set in the castle park at the edge of the Wahner Heide.

    Look for Museum of picture-book art

    Burgallee 1, 53840 Troisdorf, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Troisdorf (troisdorf.de), Naturregion Sieg

  34. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · The Rhine Corridor

    Landhaus Mönchenwerth

    A refined, long-established Rhine-side restaurant and beer garden in Meerbusch, recommended in the Michelin Guide, where chef Guy de Vries plates classic French technique brightened with Mediterranean lift right beside the river.

    Niederlöricker Straße 56, 40667 Meerbusch, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

  35. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · The Rhine Corridor

    Herzog von Burgund

    A Michelin-listed classic in a stately Neuss townhouse with a heritage staircase and a green courtyard garden — seasonal German-French cooking with a much-loved Wiener Schnitzel, the town's dependable address for a proper dinner.

    Erftstraße 88, 41460 Neuss, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

  36. Worth the detour · International & Immigrant · The Rhine Corridor

    Trattoria Enoteca

    The relaxed Italian table of Schloss Bensberg, with its own wine boutique and a vine-draped terrace: homemade pasta, coastal fish and hearty country dishes with well-matched Italian wines — fine dining's easygoing sibling to the Vendôme.

    Kadettenstraße 1, 51429 Bergisch Gladbach, Germany

    Recommended by Schlemmer Atlas, Gusto Deutschland

  37. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · The Rhine Corridor

    Restaurant Dröppelminna

    A cosy half-timbered house in Herrenstrunden serving the full Bergische Kaffeetafel — 'Koffedrenken met allem Dröm un Draan', coffee from the Dröppelmina pot with sweet-and-savoury spreads, rice pudding and hot-cherry waffles — the Bergisches Land's great hospitality ritual.

    Herrenstrunden 3, 51465 Bergisch Gladbach, Germany

    Recommended by Das Bergische (Naturarena Bergisches Land), Naturpark Bergisches Land

  38. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · The Rhine Corridor

    Gasthaus Zur Quelle der Strunde

    For nearly 150 years an inn among the meadows at the source of the Strunde, famous for its Bergische Kaffeetafel and Sunday Bergische Waffeln — coffee, cocoa and a closing schnapps included, served over a long, unhurried afternoon.

    Herrenstrunden 31, 51465 Bergisch Gladbach, Germany

    Recommended by Bürgerportal Bergisch Gladbach (in-gl.de), Das Bergische (Naturarena Bergisches Land)

  39. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · The Rhine Corridor

    Weingut Pieper — Vinothek

    A defining family winery of the Siebengebirge, working ten hectares on the Drachenfels — a volcanic trachyte soil found in no other German wine region. Taste the Drachenfels Rieslings and reds in the Königswinter vinothek, the corridor's own wine.

    Hauptstraße 458, 53639 Königswinter, Germany

    Recommended by Bonn Tourismus (visit-bonn-region.de), Falstaff

155 sights and 106 places to eat across the lower-Rhine triangle — Cologne (the UNESCO Dom, twelve Romanesque churches, and the Kölsch brewhouses), Bonn (Beethoven and the Museumsmeile) and Düsseldorf (the Altstadt “longest bar in the world”, Altbier, the Kö and Little Tokyo). A canon from Halve Hahn and Himmel un Ääd to Japanese ramen, out to a deep Michelin bench.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The Rhineland canon is Kölsch and Altbier brewhouse culture (Cologne pours Kölsch, Düsseldorf pours Alt — a real rivalry), Halve Hahn, Himmel un Ääd, Rheinischer Sauerbraten and Flönz, plus Düsseldorf’s Little Tokyo ramen/izakaya bench and a deep Michelin roster. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched in-language and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, Gault&Millau, the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger, Express, Rheinische Post, the General-Anzeiger Bonn, WDR, Der Feinschmecker/Falstaff, the city tourism boards, DW Travel and vetted local creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
